strings.name: Riken Yamamoto
strings.summary: Born in Beijing and raised in Yokohama, Yamamoto studied at Nihon University and Tokyo University of the Arts. He founded his practice in 1973, exploring connections between private life and public space through housing, schools, libraries and museums. He emphasizes transparent boundaries and neighborly interaction and promoted community research after the earthquake. Awarded the 2024 Pritzker Prize, his practice connects architectural form with residents’ everyday encounters.

strings.influence.rationale: Through housing and public buildings, he explores spatial relationships between families and society and continually advances architectural practice centered on community interaction.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Architecture graduate, Nihon University (1968); architecture master’s degree, Tokyo University of the Arts (1971).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Between public and private
strings.highlights.h1.text: Open boundaries and shared spaces enable neighborly interaction in housing and public buildings.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Pritzker Architecture Prize
strings.highlights.h2.text: The 2024 award recognized his sustained architectural attention to community relationships.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Wins Pritzker Prize
strings.timeline.t1.text: His sustained exploration of architecture and community earned the 2024 prize.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Creates Local Republic Award
strings.timeline.t2.text: Established an award encouraging young architects concerned with local society and public life.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Promotes community research
strings.timeline.t3.text: After the Great East Japan Earthquake, established Local Area Republic Labo to support community activities through design.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Hotakubo Housing
strings.timeline.t4.text: Completed the Kumamoto housing project, organizing relationships between residents through a shared courtyard.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Builds GAZEBO home
strings.timeline.t5.text: Used terraces and rooftops in Yokohama to explore interaction between a home and its neighbors.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Establishes practice
strings.timeline.t6.text: Founded Riken Yamamoto & Field Shop, later expanding from housing into educational and cultural buildings.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns architecture master’s
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed postgraduate architectural training at Tokyo University of the Arts.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes undergraduate studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated in architecture from Nihon University before continuing his studies.
